newsitem.title: CANADA: Petro-Canada plans C$950 mln 1997 spending.
newsitem.headline: Petro-Canada plans C$950 mln 1997 spending.

text.p: Petro-Canada said on Thursday it planned to invest C$950 million in property, plant, equipment and exploration in 1997.
The total would be about the same as Petro-Canada's estimated 1996 spending, excluding its acquisition earlier this year of Amerada Hess Canada for C$735 million.

"Petro-Canada will continue its strong capital investment program in 1997, primarily to exploit attractive growth opportunities within our core businesses," Petro-Canada chief executive Jim Stanford said in a statement.
"We expect to fund this program from cash flow and will maintain our financial strength and flexibility."

Petro-Canada said it would allocate about C$350 million to upstream operations in Western Canada, including C$125 million for exploration and C$170 million for development of conventional oil and gas properties.
Spending on development and exploration off Canada's east coast, including the Hibernia and Terra Nova projects, was expected to total C$190 million next year.
It said C$100 million of capitalized lease obligations, related to a Hibernia tanker, was expected to be added to company accounts in 1997.

Petro-Canada said more than C$60 million would be spent outside Canada, mostly to complete development of the Njord oil field in Norway and further exploration and development on the two-million-acre Tinrhert Block in Algeria.

Outlays in the company's downstream division for 1997 were pegged at C$215 million, mainly to speed the enhancement of retail marketing operations and to improve the efficiency and profitability of refineries and its recently expanded lubricants operation in Mississauga, Ontario.
Of the downstream total, about C$35 million was earmarked for meeting legislated product specifications and further improving environmental, health and safety performance.
